item.title: Home repairs and tools
item.description: Learn words for simple jobs at home, such as hanging a picture, tightening a screw and replacing a worn handle. Practise using these words in common phrases.

children.definition: To put something up so that it is held from the top.
children.example: We need to hang a small mirror by the front door.

children.definition: A curved or bent piece that holds things such as keys or coats.
children.example: I put my keys on the hook by the door.

children.definition: A separate border, often made of wood, metal or plastic, that holds a picture or photo.
children.example: I put the school photo in a wooden frame.
collocations: put a photo in a frame

children.definition: A piece fixed under a shelf to hold it up.
children.example: The metal bracket under the shelf is loose.

children.definition: A thin piece of metal with a sharp point that you hit with a tool to hold something in place.
children.example: There was already a nail in the wall, so I hung my small picture there.

children.definition: A tool with a heavy head that you use to hit things such as nails.
children.example: I used a hammer to tap a nail into the wall.

children.definition: A small, usually metal piece with a raised line that winds around it. You turn it to fasten things together.
children.example: One of the screws fell out of the kitchen drawer handle.

children.definition: A tool with a handle and a long metal part that you use to turn screws.
children.example: I used a small screwdriver to tighten a screw in my glasses.

children.definition: To turn a screw, nut or similar part so it holds more firmly.
children.example: I tightened the screw on the cupboard door handle.

children.definition: Able to move because it is not fixed firmly or does not fit tightly.
children.example: The bathroom door handle feels loose when I turn it.

children.definition: To take away an old or broken thing and put another one in its place.
children.example: We replaced the old rubber feet on the stool.
collocations: replace something with a new one

children.definition: In poor condition after being used a lot.
children.example: We bought a new doormat because the old one was worn.

children.definition: The part of something that you hold to open, move or use it.
children.example: I bought a new handle for the top drawer.

children.definition: To make something work properly again when it is broken or does not work as it should.
children.example: My sister fixed the drawer, and now it closes easily.
